markscheme: **D.** Cu goes from +2 to 0 (reduced, loses oxygen); H goes from 0 to +1 (oxidised, gains oxygen). H₂ is the reducing agent.

prompt: Write half-equations for the reduction of MnO₄⁻ to Mn²⁺ in acid and the oxidation of Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺, and combine them into an overall equation.
markscheme:
MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O **(A1)**; Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻ **(A1)**

MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5Fe²⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O **(A1)** — electrons balanced by multiplying the iron half-equation by 5.

concept: Ease of oxidation and reduction in a group
prompt: Chlorine water is added to potassium bromide solution. Write the ionic equation and explain the reaction in terms of the position of the halogens in group 17.
markscheme: Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + Br₂ (orange solution) **(A1)**; chlorine is a stronger oxidising agent: it is smaller, so it attracts electrons more strongly than bromine **(R1)**

prompt: Write the ionic equation for zinc reacting with hydrochloric acid, and identify the species oxidised.
markscheme: Zn + 2H⁺ → Zn²⁺ + H₂ **(A1)**; zinc is oxidised (0 → +2) **(A1)**

prompt: In every electrochemical cell, oxidation occurs at the:
options: positive electrode in both cell types
markscheme: **A.** Oxidation always occurs at the anode and reduction at the cathode, in both voltaic and electrolytic cells (the signs of the electrodes differ between the two types).

prompt: For a Zn/Zn²⁺ and Cu/Cu²⁺ voltaic cell, identify the anode, the direction of electron flow, and the function of the salt bridge.
markscheme: Zinc is the anode (more reactive, oxidised) **(A1)**; electrons flow from Zn to Cu through the external wire **(A1)**; the salt bridge allows ions to move to maintain charge balance and complete the circuit **(A1)**

prompt: Explain how a lithium-ion battery can be recharged, and state one advantage of rechargeable cells.
markscheme: An external power supply forces the redox reactions to run in reverse, restoring the original reactants **(R1)**; they can be reused many times, reducing waste and cost **(A1)**

prompt: State the products at each electrode in the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, with half-equations.
markscheme: Cathode: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na **(A1)**; anode: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻ **(A1)**; electrical energy drives a non-spontaneous reaction **(R1)**

prompt:
Ethanol is heated with acidified potassium dichromate(VI).

**(a)** State the colour change. **[1]**

**(b)** Explain how the conditions determine whether ethanal or ethanoic acid is obtained. **[2]**

**(c)** Explain why 2-methylpropan-2-ol is not oxidised. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Orange to green **(A1)**

**(b)** Distil immediately to remove ethanal (bp 21 °C) before further oxidation **(A1)**; heat under reflux to oxidise fully to ethanoic acid **(A1)**

**(c)** It is a tertiary alcohol: the carbon bearing OH has no hydrogen atom to lose **(R1)**

prompt: Name the product when propanone is reduced with sodium borohydride, and the type of alcohol formed.
markscheme: Propan-2-ol **(A1)**; a secondary alcohol (ketones reduce to secondary, aldehydes to primary alcohols) **(A1)**

prompt: State the conditions for the hydrogenation of ethene, and one industrial use of hydrogenation.
markscheme: H₂ with a nickel catalyst at about 150 °C (or Pt/Pd at room temperature) **(A1)**; converting vegetable oils into solid fats (margarine) **(A1)**

prompt: Describe the standard hydrogen electrode and explain why it is needed.
markscheme: H₂ gas at 100 kPa bubbled over platinum in 1.0 mol dm⁻³ H⁺ at 298 K **(A1)**; the potential of a single electrode cannot be measured alone, so all electrode potentials are measured relative to this reference, defined as 0 V **(R1)**

prompt: Calculate $E^{\ominus}_{cell}$ for a Zn/Cu cell ($E^{\ominus}$: Zn²⁺/Zn −0.76 V, Cu²⁺/Cu +0.34 V) and state whether the reaction is spontaneous.
Calculate ΔG° for the Zn/Cu cell reaction ($E^{\ominus}_{cell}=1.10$ V, $F=96\,500\ \text{C mol}^{-1}$).
Predict the products at each electrode for the electrolysis of **(a)** concentrated aqueous NaCl and **(b)** aqueous CuSO₄ with inert electrodes. Explain the cathode product in (a).
markscheme:
**(a)** Cathode: H₂; anode: Cl₂ **(A1)**. Water is reduced in preference to Na⁺ because its reduction potential is much less negative **(R1)**

**(b)** Cathode: Cu; anode: O₂ (water oxidised, as sulfate is not) **(A1)**

prompt: Describe how a spoon is electroplated with silver.
markscheme: The spoon is the cathode and a silver bar is the anode, in a solution of a silver salt (e.g. AgNO₃) **(A1)**; Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag deposits on the spoon while the anode dissolves, keeping [Ag⁺] constant **(A1)**
